examples.question_text: Sketch $y=\arcsin x$ by reflecting the principal restricted sine graph in $y=x$. State its domain, range, asymptotes, parity and whether it is increasing or decreasing. Mark the point corresponding to $\left(-\frac{\pi}{6},-\frac12\right)$ on the restricted sine graph.

Sketch $y=\arccos x$ by reflecting the principal restricted cosine graph in $y=x$. State its domain, range, asymptotes, parity and whether it is increasing or decreasing. Mark the point corresponding to $\left(\frac{2\pi}{3},-\frac12\right)$ on the restricted cosine graph.
Sketch $y=\arctan x$ by reflecting $y=\tan x$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$ in $y=x$. Show its asymptotes, state its domain and range, and mark the point where $x=-1$.
On the interval $-\frac12\le x\le\frac12$, sketch $y=\arcsin x$ and $y=\arccos x$ on the same axes. By adding ordinates, sketch $y=\arcsin x+\arccos x$ on that interval, including its endpoints.
